questions.question: Distinguish between a cash sale and a credit sale and explain why debtors are an asset. Give one advantage and one disadvantage of selling on credit.
questions.expected_answer: Cash sale: the customer pays immediately. Credit sale: goods are delivered now and paid for later; the customer becomes a debtor. Debtors are an asset because the business has a right to receive the money (a current asset). Advantage (any one): more sales, customer loyalty, larger orders. Disadvantage (any one): waiting for money (cash flow), bad debts, extra administration.

questions.question: State three rights of consumers and one duty of credit providers under the National Credit Act (Act 34 of 2005).
questions.expected_answer: Consumer rights (any three): to apply for credit without unfair discrimination; to be told reasons for refusal; to receive information in plain language, including the full cost before signing; a free credit report from each bureau once a year and the right to correct it; confidentiality. Credit provider duty: carry out an affordability assessment and not engage in reckless lending (also disclose costs, charge within limits).

questions.question: A television costs R6 000 cash or 12 monthly payments of R650. Calculate the total credit price, the cost of credit and the cost as a percentage of the cash price.
questions.expected_answer: Total credit price = 12 × 650 = R7 800. Cost of credit = 7 800 - 6 000 = R1 800. Percentage = 1 800 ÷ 6 000 × 100 = 30 percent.
